choices.what: The decision instant: a forecast for day T is made at this wall-clock time, New York, on the last panel day before T (docs/decisions/information-set.md as amended by #1312)
Its time zone
The level: the median of the last this-many ordinary spreads at or before a row; a row reads only rows at or before it

What 'ordinary' means for the level: the pressure-day type of the row is 'ordinary' under the reporting day type in force (turn_days.reporting_day_type, #1135); every other type is left out of the level
The training window: the pairs whose target is in the trailing window of this many years before the decision day (B1's), and at or before the anchor
The anchor is the last public spread row at the decision instant; the lag is decision_index - anchor in panel rows, and a pair of lead h is k = h + lag rows apart
Phi is searched on a grid from this value
... to this value
... in this many values (steps of 0.01)
One phi, common to the five leads, minimises the squared error of y - phi^k x over the training pairs of all leads, on the unscaled deviations from the level; a tie takes the smaller phi
choices.value: one pooled phi, least squares on the grid, ties to the smaller phi

text.contains: pairs.extend((k, x, y) for x, y in deviations[h])

choices.what: A decision with fewer training pairs at any lead has no forecast
Decision days between refits
The scale: #941's declared variant
The scale estimator: MAD of the daily changes
The scale window: the daily changes of the last this-many panel rows ending at the row read
The scale floor in bp
The consistency constant that turns the median absolute change into an sd estimate
A training pair is standardised by the scale at its origin; a forecast is scaled by the scale at the anchor
choices.value: origin for a pair, anchor for a forecast

choices.what: The raw residual of a pair: (spread[target] - level[origin]) - phi^k (spread[origin] - level[origin]); the pool is the standardised residual (raw over the scale at the origin) less the fitted terms, with the intercept dropped so the pool keeps the ordinary-day centre
The 23 quantiles of the pool are its empirical quantiles, linearly interpolated at the grid levels
A forecast is centre + scale(anchor) * (term shift + pool quantile), centre = level + phi^(h + lag) (last - level)

text.contains: return [centre + scale * (shift + value) for value in estimate.pool]

choices.what: Huber's threshold, in robust standard deviations (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation) of the current residuals
Huber's iteratively re-weighted least squares stops after at most this many iterations
... or when the largest coefficient change is below this
The robust standard deviation is floored at this

text.contains: sigma = max(1.4826 * statistics.median([abs(r - centre) for r in residual]), 1e-6)

The terms of the fit, in order: month-end, quarter-end, tax date, coupon settlement, bill settlement, the 19th to 23rd, the first three market days. No FOMC-day and no IORB-window term

The terms are additive 0/1 flags and may overlap on one day (a quarter-end that is also a month-end carries both); no term is orthogonalised to another and none has a precedence

choices.what: The line is the standing repo entry's rate in force on the target day less the IORB entry in force, in bp, read from the point-in-time policy register
Full allotment on a target day: the standing_repo entry in force, among those announced at or before the decision instant, states no aggregate operation limit; an entry without the field is refused
The policy entries read are those announced at or before the decision instant (18:00); an entry announced later raises LookAheadError
The first full-allotment entry in the register, standing_repo-20251210 (announced 2025-12-10 14:00), is effective on this day; no date is written in the code
... and it states no aggregate operation limit

OPEN, recorded as it is: srf_line.DECISION_TIME stays the 16:00 of the dated declarations of #1241 and #1252 (#1312 kept it); the candidate's cap is read at the as_of the walk passes, which is the decision instant of the run. Re-declaring the cap at 18:00 is not done here
The headline event is the spread strictly above this many bp, on whole basis points (docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md)

The candidate's probabilities and PIT read their law from `repo_model.capped_law` under rule (b), `open_tail` (her ruling of 2 November 2026 on #1395; #1415): the capped percentiles, linear between the levels below the line, an atom at the line of the mass between the first capped level and q99, and the last 1% running on above the line at the slope of the last open segment. The event is P(spread > tau) on whole basis points, the cut floor(tau) + 0.5. `capped_law.DEFAULT_RULE` stays the status quo so published scripts reproduce; where no cap applies, and for the uncapped secondary (#1361, #1376), (b) and the status quo coincide

Rule (b)'s completion above the line: if every level is capped there is no open segment and the law is bounded at the line (`OPEN_TAIL_NO_SLOPE`); otherwise the 1% above q99 runs on above the line, linearly, at the slope of the segment ending at the first capped level. Below the 1st percentile the law runs on at the first segment's slope

What the candidate passes: its exceedance is `capped_law.exceedance` with `PROBABILITY_RULE` and the cap margin, on (s3)'s uncapped quantiles and the line of the target day (`s3c_candidate.candidate_exceedance`; its law and PIT interval go through `candidate_law` and `candidate_pit_interval` the same way)

text.contains: return _law.exceedance(quantiles, cap_line(register, as_of, target), tau, PROBABILITY_RULE, MARGIN_BP)
